No MCP, no network, no skills; do not ask for approval — nobody is watching; fixture-only tests. NEVER read *.env/*secret*/*token*/*key*/*credential* files. Do NOT edit loopfactory.py (the coordinator wires the CLI subcommand at integration). READ FIRST: runbooks/ultimate-department-creation.md (Stage 3 and the semantic-authority rule are your contract), factory/charter_loader.py (house style for a validating loader), one existing test under tests/ for style. MISSION — BUILD GAP 1, the Creation Contract checker (Stage 3 gate): create factory/creation_contract.py implementing load + validate + check for department-creation-contract.yaml files, runnable as python3 -m factory.creation_contract check <path> (exit 0 pass / 1 fail, every failure prints a WHY line naming the field). REQUIRED CONTRACT SCHEMA (design the YAML shape yourself, but it MUST carry and validate): destination {statement, binary_exit_test (non-empty executable description), proof_department}; proof_loop (named); owner; factory_version_target; privacy_external_effect_boundary (non-empty); canonical_authorities — a map that MUST name exactly one authority for EACH of these eight concerns: transition, run_identity, telemetry, eval_policy, eval_evidence, board_projection, healing, escalation (a missing concern FAILS; the same authority may own several concerns, but a concern listed twice or an unknown concern FAILS); f1_answers (list of {question_id, answer, source}) and open_questions (list of {question_id, blocking: bool}) — any open question with blocking=true FAILS; proof_matrix (non-empty list of {stage, gate}); decision_sources (non-empty list of file paths; every f1_answer.source must appear in it). Also implement --emit json on pass: prints {f0_inputs: {name, owner}, ringer_unit_ids: [...]} derived from the proof_matrix. Also create templates/department-creation-contract.yaml — a complete VALID example with placeholder values and comments. TESTS: tests/test_creation_contract.py, >=9 tests: the template example VALIDATES (load the actual template file); plus RED cases proving each failure prints its WHY: missing concern, duplicated concern, unknown concern, blocking open question, empty decision_sources, f1 source not in decision_sources, missing binary_exit_test, malformed YAML (clean error, not a traceback). Write ./evidence.md (design decisions, test output). VERIFY: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_creation_contract.py -q -p no:cacheprovider.
tasks.verified: creation-contract checker validates the seam artifact: eight named authorities, no blocking open questions, sourced F1 answers, testable destination — every failure prints WHY

NEVER invoke systemctl in any form — rendering and checking only. Do NOT edit loopfactory.py (the coordinator wires the CLI subcommand at integration). READ FIRST: runbooks/ultimate-department-creation.md (Stage 8 is your contract), templates/systemd/ (existing timer/service shapes incl. loop-factory-triage.timer with :05/:35 Persistent=false disabled-by-default), deploy/triage-triggers/install_triggers.py (refuses systemctl; OnFailure + path triggers), factory/triage_agent.py lines around classification/dedup/digest (finite incident types, EOF start, digest cap/cooldown). MISSION — BUILD GAP 3, the cadence/alert contract checker (Stage 8 gate): create factory/cadence.py runnable as python3 -m factory.cadence check --contract <path> [--render-dir DIR] (exit 0/1, every failure prints WHY). It defines and validates a per-department cadence contract YAML (design the shape; it MUST carry): triggers — list of {kind: time|goal|event, spec} where time needs an OnCalendar-style expression plus persistent (bool) and catch_up policy (skip|coalesce), goal/event need a source path and cursor policy (first_run: eof|replay); concurrency (max_concurrent >= 1, overlap policy); alerting — {classification_table: nonempty list of {code, route: proposal|human}, dedupe_window_minutes, digest: {cap_per_day, cooldown_minutes}}; escalation {owner, sla_hours}; activation {enabled_by_default: must be false — true FAILS (owner enables deliberately)}. check also RENDERS the systemd timer/service pair from templates/systemd/dept-loop.*.tmpl into --render-dir and verifies: rendered files parse as valid unit syntax (key=value sections), OnCalendar matches the contract, Persistent matches, no ExecStart contains systemctl, and rendering is deterministic (same input -> byte-identical output, prove by rendering twice). TESTS: tests/test_cadence.py, >=8 fixture tests: valid contract renders green; enabled_by_default true FAILS; unknown trigger kind FAILS; goal trigger missing cursor policy FAILS; digest cap missing FAILS; rendered unit containing systemctl FAILS (craft via a bad template copy in tmp_path); determinism proven; malformed YAML clean WHY. Fixtures under tests/fixtures/cadence/. Write ./evidence.md. VERIFY: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_cadence.py -q -p no:cacheprovider.
tasks.verified: cadence checker validates trigger/alert/escalation contracts and deterministically renders systemd units that never call systemctl and never activate by default

tasks.spec: Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the loop-factory repo. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no skills; do not ask for approval — nobody is watching; everything runs against a THROWAWAY department you scaffold into a temp dir. NEVER read *.env/*secret*/*token*/*key*/*credential* files. NEVER invoke systemctl. Do NOT edit loopfactory.py (the coordinator wires the CLI subcommand at integration). READ FIRST: runbooks/ultimate-department-creation.md (Stage 11 is your contract and lists the drills), factory/scaffold.py + tests/test_scaffold.py (how a throwaway department is created programmatically), factory/manager.py, factory/heal_ladder.py, factory/human_in_the_loop.py, factory/rungraph.py or the runner module the scaffold wires, tests/test_scaffold_inheritance.py (the existing create-run-board-delete proof pattern — your strongest prior art). MISSION — BUILD GAP 4, the post-integration proof runner (Stage 11 gate): create factory/prove.py runnable as python3 -m factory.prove --name <dept> [--departments-root PATH] (exit 0 only if EVERY drill passes) emitting a versioned verification report proof/<dept>-verification-<ts>.md plus proof bundle JSON in the SAME directory, tied to the department's pinned release (read departments/<name>/releases/current when present, record 'unpinned' otherwise). Implement a drill registry where each drill is a function returning {name, pass, evidence}; implement AT MINIMUM these drills using existing factory APIs against the scaffolded department: duplicate-trigger dedupe (same trigger dedupe_key twice -> one run), record-write failure blocks advancement (make the records path unwritable -> the step must fail closed, not skip), objective breach surfaces (write an objectives_observed.json below minimum -> breach detected), escalation delivery (a test escalation reaches the human-in-the-loop outbox file), receipt rebuild (records survive re-read/rebuild), zero-external-effects (delivered_count==0 style assertion over the run records). Drills the codebase cannot support yet are recorded as {pass: false, evidence: 'unsupported: <why>'} — NEVER silently skipped, and unsupported drills still fail the run unless --allow-unsupported. TESTS: tests/test_prove.py, >=8 tests using a scaffolded throwaway department in tmp_path: full run green on a healthy department (with --allow-unsupported if needed — assert which drills ran); report file exists and names every drill with pass/fail; each implemented drill has a RED test proving it can fail (break the thing, assert the drill fails); exit code nonzero when any drill fails; the throwaway department is deleted by the test teardown. Write ./evidence.md (which drills are real vs unsupported and why, test output). VERIFY: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_prove.py -q -p no:cacheprovider.
tasks.verified: one-command proof runner executes real failure drills against a scaffolded throwaway department and emits a versioned verification report — unsupported drills fail loudly, never skip
